title: Residual: hardcoded FOUNDER_WALLET_EXPECTED still bricks the loop on legitimate wallet rotation; the prod-mode test mutates real founder state (snapshot/restore is race-prone and not crash-safe)
description: Two non-blocking residuals. (1) FIND-404 carry-over: the prod wallet pin is now SAFE as defense-in-depth because the prod root is env-independent (record-earn.mjs:25), so wallet.json can only ever be the canonical founder wallet and the pin at line 48 can only match the real wallet — the FIND-401 HOME-plant attack is dead. BUT the duplicated source literal (line 42) still means a legitimate gen-wallet re-run / key rotation / new-host re-provision changes wallet.json.address while the constant does not, permanently dieing at line 48 with a message that reads like an attack ('must be the PINNED founder wallet') rather than config drift. This is availability, not integrity — acceptable for a single-host founder, but should bind the pin at provisioning (a write-once FOUNDER_DIR/.wallet-pin) instead of a source literal. (2) NEW: the prod-mode behavioral case (test-record-earn.sh:85-92) runs the REAL prod script against the REAL /Users/anicca/.anicca-founder, then snapshots /Users/anicca/.anicca-founder/state/usdc-baseline.txt (line 89) and restores it (line 92). This is not crash-safe: if the test process is killed between the prod run and line 92, or if the prod run on the real wallet observes a real on-chain INCREASE (delta>0) and appends a REAL row + advances the real baseline, the restore at line 92 rolls the live baseline BACKWARD to the pre-test value while leaving the just-appended ledger row in place — that exact row can then be re-counted on the next real wake (replay sees the restored-lower baseline). It also races any concurrent real wake-loop invocation sharing the same baseline file (no lock). The test should run the prod-mode assertion against a throwaway root or assert purely on the planted HOME dir staying empty WITHOUT touching the real baseline at all; touching live money-loop state from a test is a hygiene violation (cf. project rule: test cleanup must never broaden to shared/real state).

evidence.snippet:
RB="/Users/anicca/.anicca-founder/state/usdc-baseline.txt"; BK=""; [ -f "$RB" ] && BK="$(cat "$RB" 2>/dev/null)"
HOME="$PLANT" node "$M" >/dev/null 2>&1
ok "$([ ! -s "$PLANT/.anicca-founder/state/earn-ledger.jsonl" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)" "PROD: HOME-poisoned planted dir NOT used as root (no fabricated row) — FIND-401"
[ -n "$BK" ] && printf '%s' "$BK" > "$RB" 2>/dev/null  # restore the real founder baseline if the prod run touched it

fix: (1) Bind the wallet pin at provisioning: gen-wallet writes a write-once /Users/anicca/.anicca-founder/.wallet-pin; record-earn.mjs compares wallet.json.address to that file instead of the source literal (line 42), so rotation does not brick the loop and the address is not a source-readable recipe. (2) Make the prod-mode test NON-mutating of live state: assert ONLY that the planted HOME dir's ledger stays empty (the prod literal root is proven un-movable by that alone). Do NOT run the real script against the real baseline; if a prod-literal run is wanted, point the literal at a temp clone or assert the prod run is a no-op via a read-only check. Remove the snapshot/restore of /Users/anicca/.anicca-founder/state/usdc-baseline.txt (lines 89,92) entirely — it can roll the live baseline backward and enable a real-row replay double-count.
